events.body:
## Upgrade vulnerable dependencies

This PR upgrades **2** packages in `authkit` with known security advisories, each to the release that fixes the most of them while being at least 7 days old (brand-new releases are where supply-chain attacks land).

| Package | From | To | Released | Fixes | Still open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PyJWT` | 1.7.1 | **2.14.0** | 47 days ago | [CVE-2026-101917](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-101917), [CVE-2026-32597](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-32597), [CVE-2026-102267](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102267), [CVE-2026-102268](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102268), [CVE-2022-29217](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-29217), [CVE-2026-102269](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102269) and 6 more | - |
| `requests` | 2.31.0 | **2.33.0** | 216 days ago | [CVE-2024-47081](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-47081), [CVE-2024-35195](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-35195), [CVE-2026-25645](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-25645) | - |

### Dependency files

- `requirements.txt`: the pins, edited in place

### What changed upstream

Quoted from each package's own changelog (found and read with Tavily), for the releases between the two versions:

- **PyJWT** 1.7.1 → 2.14.0: 18 releases, from [PyJWT changelog](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.rst)
  - 2.0.0: “Drop support for Python 2 and Python 3.0-3.5”
  - 2.0.0: “Drop support for PyCrypto and ECDSA”
  - 2.0.0: “Dropped deprecated errors”
  - 2.0.0: “Dropped deprecated `verify_expiration` param in `jwt.decode(...)`”
  - 2.0.0: “Dropped deprecated `verify` param in `jwt.decode(...)`”
  - 2.0.0: “Dropped deprecated `require_*` options in `jwt.decode(...)`”
  - 2.0.0: “Python 3.5 is EOL so we decide to drop its support. Version `1.7.1` is the last one supporting Python 3.0-3.5.”
  - 2.0.0: “Dropped the included cli entry point.”
- **requests** 2.31.0 → 2.33.0: 7 releases, from [requests changelog](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/HEAD/HISTORY.md)
  - 2.32.0: “Requests has officially dropped support for CPython 3.7 (#6642)”
  - 2.32.0: “Requests has officially dropped support for PyPy 3.7 and 3.8 (#6641)”
  - 2.32.0: “Requests now supports optional use of character detection (`chardet` or `charset_normalizer`) when repackaged or vendored. This enables `pip` and other projects to minimize their vendoring surface area. The `Response.text()` and `apparent_encoding` APIs will default to `utf-8` if neither library is…”
  - 2.32.2: “To provide a more stable migration for custom HTTPAdapters impacted by the CVE changes in 2.32.0, we've renamed `_get_connection` to a new public API, `get_connection_with_tls_context`. Existing custom HTTPAdapters will need to migrate their code to use this new API. `get_connection` is considered…”
  - 2.32.4: “Dropped support for pypy 3.9 following its end of support.”
  - 2.32.5: “Dropped support for Python 3.8 following its end of support.”
  - 2.33.0: “Dropped support for Python 3.9 following its end of support. (#7196)”

### Tests

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before the upgrade | ✅ 5 passed, 10 warnings in 0.17s |
| After the version bump | ❌ 4 failed, 1 passed, 4 warnings in 0.23s |
| After OpenPort's fix | ✅ 5 passed, 8 warnings in 0.18s |

### Code changes

The upgrade broke the tests, so Nemotron Super changed the application code (never the tests):

- `authkit/tokens.py`: PyJWT 2.0.0 changed jwt.encode to return strings (not bytes) and requires explicit algorithms in jwt.decode.
  - Based on [PyJWT changelog](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.rst): “Tokens are returned as string instead of a byte string”
  - Based on [PyJWT changelog](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.rst): “Require explicit ``algorithms`` in ``jwt.decode(...)`` by default”

---
Opened by OpenPort. Never auto-merged: review the changes and the test results above.
